statement: Let \(a > b > c > d\) be positive integers satisfying \(a + b + c + d = 502\) and \(a^2 - b^2 + c^2 - d^2 = 502\). Calculate how many possible values of \(a\) there are.

On Babba Island they use a two-letter alphabet, \(a\) and \(b\), and every finite sequence of letters is a word. For each set \(P\) of six words of 4 letters each, let \(N_P\) be the set of all words that do not contain any word of \(P\) as a subword. Prove that if \(N_P\) is finite, then all its words have length at most 10, and find a set \(P\) such that \(N_P\) is finite and contains at least one word of length 10.
Let \(a\) be a real number such that \(\dfrac{1}{a} = a - \lfloor a \rfloor\). Show that \(a\) is irrational.

A positive integer is called a winner if it can be written as the sum of a perfect square and a perfect cube. For example, \(33 = 5^2 + 2^3\) is a winner. Gabriel chooses two positive integers \(r\) and \(s\), and Germán must find 2005 positive integers \(n\) such that for each \(n\), both \(r + n\) and \(s + n\) are winners. Prove that Germán can always achieve this.

Let \(AM\) and \(AN\) be the tangent lines from an external point \(A\) to a circle \(\Gamma\), with \(M, N\) on the circle. A line through \(A\) meets \(\Gamma\) at \(B\) and \(C\) (with \(B\) between \(A\) and \(C\)), and \(\dfrac{AB}{BC} = \dfrac{2}{3}\). If \(P\) is the intersection of line \(AB\) and line \(MN\), calculate \(\dfrac{AP}{CP}\).

Let \(k \geq 1\) be an integer. In a group of \(2k+1\) people, some are sincere (always tell the truth) and the rest are unpredictable (sometimes tell the truth, sometimes lie); the unpredictable ones number at most \(k\). An outsider must determine who is sincere and who is unpredictable by asking a sequence of questions, where in each step he chooses two people \(A\) and \(B\) and asks \(A\): "Is \(B\) sincere?". Show that after \(3k\) questions the outsider can classify all \(2k+1\) people with certainty.

Clarification: Each of the \(2k+1\) people knows who is sincere and who is unpredictable.
